text:
maria: Heads-up — I ran a set of nsys captures on a dedicated canary pool to compare full tracing vs light sampling for KV-cache heavy traffic. Results are surprising and we should pick guardrails before enabling anything in prod.

alex: Curious — what did you measure for overhead?

maria: Short summary: full trace (cuda+nvtx+osrt) with 30s windows bumped p50 token latency ~18-28% and reduced throughput ~22-33% on our Llama-variant workload when KV cache miss rate was >20%. Sampling (1s every 10s, kernel sampling enabled) looked much cheaper: p50 +3-8%, throughput loss ~5-7%, but missed a bunch of short attention kernels.

ryan: ugh that's higher than I expected for full traces. Do you have command snippets you used?

maria: Yep — ran on canary nodes only with traffic mirror. Example:
```
nsys profile --output=run_canary_1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx:profiler_start:profiler_end --force-overwrite --sample=none --duration=30
```
and for sampling:
```
nsys profile --output=run_canary_sample --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=periodic:1000us --duration=30
```
(we use a wrapper that toggles NVTX around request handling so the captures isolate serving code).

sam: Important context: the canary nodes are on the same GPU families as prod, but they were running traffic-mirror which doubles some GC pressure — ensure you warm KV cache first. Did you warm it?

maria: Yes — warmed for 5 minutes at 80% qps. The overhead still correlates with cache miss rate — when misses spike, more kernel launches occur and the trace collector ends up serializing metadata + file IO which amplifies the overhead.

alex: That matches our hypothesis: the profiler adds bookkeeping per kernel launch. For short kernels (e.g., fused-attn small-batch) the relative overhead is worse. When KV-cache hits skip many kernels and the impact is smaller.

ryan: Any kernel hotspots identified?

maria: Main hotspots in the full traces: a lot of time in NVTX serialization and file flush, plus unexpected time spent in cuBLAS/MatMul wrapper kernels for sequence lengths around 512 (we saw different kernel selection path compared to baseline). Example names: `matmul_fp16_qk`, `fused_attention_launch`, and some small kernels like `add_bias_relu` that get sampled away in low-res runs.

alex: Did you try a shorter capture window or staggered sampling to reduce overhead?

maria: Yes — 10s windows reduced the p50 hit for full traces to ~10-12% but you lose global picture. Staggered periodic sampling (capture 2s every 30s) keeps overhead near ~4% and still catches most medium-duration hotspots. But we found short noisy regressions (single-request spikes from kernel-selector bugs) rarely show up unless you capture the exact window.

sam: Proposal for safe-production profiling guardrails:
- profiler toggles only on canary or mirrored traffic by default
- default to probabilistic request-level sampling (e.g., 1/1000 requests) with option to bump to 1/100 for targeted investigations
- max concurrent capture windows per region (e.g., 2 captures)
- short capture windows (<=30s) and rate-limited captures per node
- automatic abort if p99 latency increases >10% during capture (observability alarm)
- require on-call ack to start full (non-sampling) traces

ryan: Agree. Also add KV-cache warmup requirement and record the cache hit/miss snapshot at capture start so we can correlate. We should tag traces with routing policy + model version + quantization profile.

maria: I added a small telemetry prototype — trace metadata includes `kv_cache_hit_rate`, `seq_len_dist`, `kernel_selector_version`, and `profiler_mode`. We can attach that as NVTX metadata on capture start.

alex: For locating kernel-level regressions we should:
1) run periodic low-overhead sampling across fleet (1/10k requests) to build an anomaly baseline
2) if anomaly detected, trigger canary full-trace with human approval
3) run diff of kernel timelines and aggregate per-kernel latency/launch-count deltas

maria: One example regression we found: a kernel-selection change in the new matmul heuristics caused the runtime to prefer a cutoff that routes some 512-seq matmuls to a slower kernel on A100 for small batch sizes — showed up as +12% token latency on traces. That only surfaced because we had a canary full-trace during a load test.

sam: Good to capture that in runbook. Also add enforcement: profiler start API returns a token and if the capture exceeds allowed overhead window it auto-kills and tags as aborted.

maria: I'll open a PR with the guardrail checklist and the telemetry fields + example nsys wrapper script. Also adding a dashboard tile showing "active_profiler_count" and a per-node "profiler_overhead_estimate" (derived from short probe runs).

ryan: Do we need legal/security review for NVTX payloads? We should avoid putting any user prompt text in NVTX. Only metadata keys.

maria: Agreed — masking policy: no prompt/content in traces. We only attach hashes/IDs.

tracebot: [tracebot] started nsys capture run_canary_1 on node canary-03 for trace_id=run_canary_1 — triggered by maria.

sam: OK let's iterate on the PR and add a short checklist for on-call. If anyone wants the raw trace tarballs I put them on the shared perf s3 under s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1793456789/

alex: Thanks — useful numbers. Next step: maria posts PR link and we schedule a 20m sync to finalize guardrails. :thumbsup:
